chunks: From him, from Hammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar, from Abu Basir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) that he said:
The sacrifices (of the Haruriyyah) are not permissible.

key_terms.الْحَرُورِيَّةِ: The Haruriyyah (a specific sect/group, often associated with Khawarij)

ai.seo_question: Are the sacrifices of the Haruriyyah permissible to eat according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This concise hadith from al-Isfahani establishes the impermissibility of consuming meat slaughtered by the Haruriyyah, a group often identified with the Khawarij due to their opposition to the Ahl al-Bayt. In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling underscores the principle that ritual slaughter validity is contingent not only on the act itself but also on the theological and political status of the slaughterer relative to the Imams. It serves as a key precedent for distinguishing between groups whose faith is considered valid versus those deemed apostate or distinct in their ritual practices.
